'falle' is subjunctive after 'es raro que'; 'crashes' suggests system failure, but 'fails' is more accurate (fails to function properly)
Spelling error: 'permitio' should be 'permitió' (accent mark)
English uses present perfect 'Having worked' but Spanish 'El haber trabajado' is infinitive form; more naturally 'Having worked together as a team was key...'
'carné de manejar' is regional (Latin America); in Spain typically 'carnet de conducir' or 'permiso de conducción'

'le costó el examen' means 'cost him the exam' (caused him to fail), but English says 'cost him' without object; should be 'Not having studied enough was what cost him the exam' or 'caused him to fail the exam'
'blown away' is somewhat dated slang; 'I love this series' or 'This series is amazing' more natural modern English
English phrasing 'It's a bit far for me' is awkward; 'It's a bit far' or 'It's somewhat out of the way' would be more natural. The parenthetical 'lit.' is also unnecessary for a card.
The parenthetical literal translation clutters the card. Standard presentation should be the idiom alone or followed by clean definition.
Missing 'the' before 'agreement': should be 'the points of the agreement.' Also awkward without 'the' before 'table' in context, though Spanish may omit it.
Spanish uses 'encontraba' (third person singular) but English changes to 'he encountered' without antecedent; original is impersonal/generic, not about a specific 'he'
'pan de oro' literally 'gold bread' — 'gold leaf' is correct but the term itself should note it's a calque
patrimonio de la humanidad = UNESCO World Heritage Site (not just 'a World Heritage Site')
parenthetical gloss awkwardly breaks the flow; cleaner as single sentence
parenthetical gloss interrupts idiom; better as single smooth sentence
'considerado como' = 'considered (to be)' not 'considered as'; drop 'as'
'got told off' is informal British; use 'was scolded' or 'was reprimanded' for standard register
Spanish has spelling errors ('despues'→'después', 'tome'→'tomé'); English translation correct but source is corrupted
'en la carta' = on the menu (carta = menu in restaurant context); 'in the letter' would be wrong
"dos por uno" is a 2-for-1 deal, not buy-one-get-one-free; these are different promotional structures
"Leido" is a past participle used as an absolute construction; English should be "Having read the statement" or "Once the statement had been read" for natural flow
"Llegados a este punto" is an absolute construction; "Once we crossed the border" or "After crossing the border" would be more natural than "Once the border was crossed"
The cleft construction "no es sino... como" is awkward in English; better: "It is only by working together that we will overcome this crisis" (remove "all"—awkward collocation)
awkward inversion; more natural: 'He is not without reason considered one of the best in the country' or 'There is good reason he is considered...'
missing auxiliary; should be 'Not only did he arrive late, but also poorly prepared' or 'Not only arrived late, but also poorly prepared'
awkward past perfect; more natural: 'I would have preferred that you tell me before telling mom' or 'I would have preferred you to tell me...'
carte blanche is French; English equivalent is 'blank check' or 'free rein'
literal translation in parentheses is awkward; better standalone: 'overstepped the line' or 'overstepped'
'paradise-like' is awkward; better: 'paradisiacal' or 'heavenly'

pidió el informe para hoy = asked for the report by/for today, not 'for today' in the sense of 'intended for today'; better: 'asked me for the report for today' is acceptable but 'by today' is more natural
'at eight at night' is awkward; prefer 'at eight o'clock at night' or 'at eight in the evening'
'Once the storm passed' is correct but 'After the storm passed' flows more naturally in English
desde que nació refers to the godmother's role starting from the daughter's birth, not 'since she was born' (ambiguous pronoun); should be 'since my daughter was born'
'I was left speechless' is the correct idiomatic translation of 'me quedé con la boca abierta', not 'I was left with my mouth open'
Subject is 'lo' (it/that), not 'I'; should be 'If that had been known' or 'If one had known'
'project manager' is more idiomatic as 'project lead' for 'jefe de proyecto', though acceptable
'departamento' in Latin America = apartment, but in Spain it's usually 'piso'; translation should note region or use 'flat/apartment'
'ponerse las pilas' idiom means 'to get one's act together' or 'to shape up', not just 'let's get our act together'; missing the imperative sense and idiomatic weight
Awkward phrasing; 'Approximately a century and a half ago' or 'About 150 years ago' reads more naturally in English
Translation includes unnecessary parenthetical '(lit. I put the paw in)' which violates format rules; should be 'I put my foot in it' only, or restructure without the gloss
identical to es-3876 except 'también' vs 'sino que'; both convey same meaning
'sooner' is vague; should be 'earlier' or 'before' to match 'antes'
'done the excursion' is awkward; should be 'gone on the excursion' or 'taken the excursion'
English 'makes a difference' is idiomatic; 'marks the difference' is literal/awkward phrasing
'allows machines to improve' is slightly awkward; 'enables machines to improve' reads more naturally
'the important thing is to enjoy' is correct but formal; 'what matters is enjoying' is more natural colloquially—however, both are acceptable
'perdimos la conexión del vuelo' = missed the connecting flight, not 'our connecting flight' (the flight itself, not the connection)
'jumped to greet him' implies intentional action; Spanish 'saltó a saludarlo' means 'jumped up to greet' or 'jumped to say hello'—'jumped up to greet him' is more natural
'marca personal' is more accurately 'personal brand' (noun) not 'personal branding' (gerund/process). Spanish emphasizes the brand itself, not the act of branding.
'You must present' is correct but somewhat formal; 'You need to present' or 'You should present' is more natural for bureaucratic contexts.
'Abdominales' can mean both 'sit-ups' and 'abdominal exercises' (broader). Current translation is narrower.

'Sellar en la notaría' means 'to have it sealed/certified at the notary', not 'to notarize'. Notarization is the act; sealing is the result. Should be 'to have it sealed at the notary' or 'to get it certified at the notary'.
'at nine thirty at night' is redundant. Better: 'at nine thirty in the evening' or 'at nine thirty p.m.'
'for being at home' is grammatically awkward. Better: 'for lounging at home' or 'for wearing at home'.
Spanish semicolon structure has two independent statements; English only translates first one completely. Second clause needs 'and' or period before 'compassion'.

Logical error in English translation. Spanish 'If I hadn't trusted him, he wouldn't have deceived me' is backwards—trusting someone enables deception, not prevents it. Should be 'If I had trusted him, he would have deceived me' OR the Spanish needs rechecking.
senalar (with tilde) means to point out/indicate; 'It is worth noting' requires 'conviene hacer notar' or 'es digno de mención'
'Buenas noches' is primarily 'Good night' (greeting/farewell at night); 'Good evening' is less common and requires context
'el baño' literally means bathroom; in most Spanish-speaking regions, 'el aseo', 'los servicios', or 'el WC' are more natural for public restrooms
More natural phrasing: 'La cuenta, por favor' works but 'Me trae la cuenta, por favor' or 'Quiero pedir la cuenta' is more common in restaurant contexts
